page: Microsoft Azure D48pds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dpdsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated physical cores powered by the ARM64-based Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor operating at 3.4 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 192.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance is equipped with a 2835 GB NVMe SSD, and it supports Premium Storage. It does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core capabilities and exceptional memory performance. The server achieves top-tier status in memory bandwidth tests, reaching 463.49 GB/sec for large-block read-only operations and 198.92 GB/sec for large-block writes. Multi-core performance is robust, highlighted by a Geekbench multi-core score of 22118.0 and a Passmark database operations score of 36588.41, both ranking in the top tier. However, single-core performance is more moderate, with Geekbench single-core and stress-ng single-core scores falling into the average category. Large-model LLM inference also presents a performance tradeoff, with prompt processing for a 70B model registering in the weak tier at 6.92 tokens/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM64 architecture delivers high resource density and excellent memory throughput per unit of compute resource, making it highly competitive for scale-out workloads compared to traditional x86 alternatives. The combination of 48 dedicated physical cores, a fast local NVMe SSD, and high memory bandwidth makes this server type well-suited for database operations, Redis deployments, multi-threaded software compilation, and static web serving. It is less optimal for workloads requiring specialized x86 vector extensions or heavy single-threaded execution.
